title: Types of solutions — isotonic/hyper/hypo
keyPoints: Isotonic (270-310 mOsm): NS 0.9%, RL, D5W (after glucose metabolized becomes hypotonic free water)
Hypertonic: 3% NaCl, D10W, D50W — draws water from cells
Hypotonic: 0.45% NaCl, D5W (post-metabolism) — expands cells, caution in brain injury
nursingPriority: 3% hypertonic saline 100 mL over 10 min, repeat if seizures persist, raise Na ~1-2 mEq/L/h for symptomatic only, careful monitoring to avoid osmotic demyelination.

title: Body fluid compartments
keyPoints: Total body water: 60% body weight adult (infants 75%, elderly 50%)

title: Diffusion
keyPoints: Factors: gradient, surface area, membrane thickness, molecular size
clinicalContext: Item on O2 exchange in alveoli.

title: Osmosis
keyPoints: From low to high solute concentration
nursingPriority: Toward higher solute (from dilute to concentrated).

title: Lower limb osteology
keyPoints: Femur (largest), patella, tibia, fibula, tarsals (7), metatarsals (5), phalanges (14)

title: Longest vein — great saphenous
definition: Great saphenous vein — longest in body.
keyPoints: From medial foot to femoral vein at saphenofemoral junction
Used for CABG graft, varicose vein stripping

title: Plantar flexion
definition: Pointing toes down (gastrocnemius, soleus via tibial nerve).
nursingPriority: Plantar flexion — toes down, calf muscles.

title: Upper limb — nerve supply
keyPoints: Median: thenar (ape hand, pregnant nurse sign)
clinicalContext: Patient with wrist drop post-crutch injury.
nursingPriority: Radial nerve palsy — splint, PT, EMG, usually recovers 2-3 mo.

title: Muscle origin and insertion
nursingPriority: Origin: scapula; insertion: radial tuberosity; flexes and supinates.

title: Mouth muscles
keyPoints: Innervation: facial (VII) for expression; trigeminal (V) for mastication

title: Anterior thoracic wall
clinicalContext: Item on landmark at sternal angle.
nursingPriority: Angle of Louis = T4/T5 disc, 2nd costal cartilage.

title: Abduction, adduction, eversion
clinicalContext: Item on moving leg away from body.

title: Boxer muscle (serratus anterior)
nursingPriority: Long thoracic nerve injury — physical therapy, shoulder support, usually recovers.

title: Retroperitoneal structures
keyPoints: Suprarenal gland, Aorta/IVC, Duodenum (2nd, 3rd, 4th), Pancreas (except tail), Ureters, Colon (ascending, descending), Kidneys, Esophagus (lower), Rectum

title: Adrenal gland
clinicalContext: Young patient with BP swings, headache, sweating, palpitations.
nursingPriority: Pheochromocytoma workup — plasma/urinary metanephrines, imaging; alpha-block first, then beta.

title: Growth hormone
clinicalContext: Adult with prominent jaw, enlarged hands, ring size change.
nursingPriority: Acromegaly — IGF-1, OGTT with GH, pituitary MRI; trans-sphenoidal surgery.

title: Pituitary — anterior vs posterior
keyPoints: Anterior (adenohypophysis): GH, ACTH, TSH, LH/FSH, prolactin, MSH — glandular
Posterior (neurohypophysis): ADH, oxytocin — neural (stored, not synthesized)
nursingPriority: Synthesized in hypothalamus, stored/released from posterior pituitary.

title: Thyroid hormones
keyPoints: T4 (thyroxine) most secreted; T3 more active
Follicular cells make T3/T4; parafollicular (C) cells make calcitonin
clinicalContext: Hypothyroid with TSH high T4 low.
nursingPriority: Primary hypothyroidism — levothyroxine 1.6 mcg/kg/d empty stomach, recheck TSH 6 wk.

title: Reproductive hormones
keyPoints: Menstrual cycle: follicular (FSH/E2), ovulation (LH surge), luteal (progesterone)

title: Embryonic testis to scrotum descent
definition: Testis migrates from abdominal to scrotum.
keyPoints: Undescended (cryptorchidism): infertility, testicular cancer risk; orchiopexy by 1 y
clinicalContext: 1-y-old with absent right testis in scrotum.
nursingPriority: Ultrasound to locate, refer surgery for orchiopexy before 18 mo; educate parents on malignancy risk.

title: Motilin
keyPoints: Erythromycin is a motilin agonist — used for gastroparesis
nursingPriority: Low-dose erythromycin (motilin agonist) 3 mg/kg PO TDS, dietary modification, metoclopramide.

title: Intrinsic factor of Castle
definition: From gastric parietal cells; binds B12 for ileal absorption.
keyPoints: Pernicious anemia: autoimmune destruction of parietal cells → IF deficiency → B12 deficiency
nursingPriority: Monthly IM B12 (hydroxocobalamin 1000 mcg) lifelong, diet counseling.

title: HCl secretion
keyPoints: Stimulated by: gastrin (G cells), histamine (ECL, H2), ACh (vagus)
PPIs block pump; H2 blockers compete at H2 receptor
nursingPriority: H-K ATPase (proton pump) on parietal cell.

title: Mineral absorption sites
nursingPriority: B12 deficiency likely — monthly IM B12, check bile salt diarrhea, fat-soluble vitamin status.

title: GI enzymes
keyPoints: Brush border: lactase, sucrase, maltase, peptidases
nursingPriority: Pancreatic lipase with bile salt emulsification.

title: Large intestine functions
nursingPriority: Colon (majority in SI but colon final concentration).

title: Islets of Langerhans
nursingPriority: Beta cells of islets of Langerhans.

title: Cervical vertebrae
keyPoints: C1 atlas: no body, supports skull

title: CSF — production and volume
clinicalContext: LP opening pressure 30 cm H2O in headache.
nursingPriority: Elevated ICP — consider IIH or meningitis workup, MRI, ophthalmology for papilledema, manage carefully.

title: Parasympathetic nervous system
keyPoints: Craniosacral origin: CN III, VII, IX, X and S2-S4
Effects: pupil constrict, bradycardia, bronchoconstrict, increased GI, bladder contract, sexual arousal
clinicalContext: Item on dominant tone at rest.

title: Broca vs Wernicke area
keyPoints: Broca (inferior frontal, dominant hemisphere): expressive aphasia, non-fluent, understanding preserved
Wernicke (superior temporal, dominant): receptive aphasia, fluent but nonsensical, impaired understanding
clinicalContext: Patient with fluent but meaningless speech and poor comprehension.
nursingPriority: Wernicke aphasia — speech therapy, stroke workup (temporal lobe), caregiver education on comprehension strategies.

title: Sympathetic nervous system
keyPoints: NT: ACh pre, NE post (except sweat glands ACh)
Effects: pupil dilate, tachycardia, bronchodilate, decreased GI, sweat, vasoconstrict

topic: Root values of reflexes (knee jerk L3-L4)
title: Root values of reflexes (knee jerk L3-L4)
Brachial and cervical plexus
keyPoints: Cervical plexus: C1-C4, phrenic nerve (C3-C5 keeps diaphragm alive)
Brachial plexus: C5-T1, roots-trunks-divisions-cords-branches (Real Teenagers Drink Cold Beer)
Terminal branches: axillary, radial, musculocutaneous, median, ulnar

title: Thermoregulatory center (hypothalamus)
keyPoints: Set point can be elevated by pyrogens (fever)

title: Cranial nerves — 12
keyPoints: I olfactory, II optic, III oculomotor, IV trochlear, V trigeminal, VI abducens, VII facial, VIII vestibulocochlear, IX glossopharyngeal, X vagus, XI accessory, XII hypoglossal
Mnemonic: Some Say Marry Money But My Brother Says Big Brains Matter More (sensory/motor/both)
nursingPriority: Central (UMN) VII lesion (stroke) — forehead spared due to bilateral cortical input; workup stroke.

title: Plantar reflex
keyPoints: Babinski positive: big toe dorsiflexion + fanning — UMN lesion
clinicalContext: Post-stroke patient with big toe dorsiflexion on sole stimulation.
nursingPriority: Babinski sign (UMN lesion) — consistent with stroke; document, rehabilitation.

title: Arterial supply of lung
keyPoints: Pulmonary artery: deoxygenated from RV — gas exchange
Bronchial artery: oxygenated from aorta — nutrient supply to bronchi
clinicalContext: Item on nutrient artery of lung.

title: Diaphragm physiology
keyPoints: Contracts → flattens → increased thoracic volume → inspiration
Quiet breathing mostly diaphragm; forced uses accessory muscles
nursingPriority: Diaphragm (primary) with some external intercostal activity.

title: Visceral pleura
keyPoints: Sensory innervation: visceral autonomic (pain not felt), parietal somatic (sharp pain)

title: Cricoid cartilage
definition: Only complete cartilaginous ring in airway.
keyPoints: Sellick maneuver (cricoid pressure) in RSI (no longer routine)
clinicalContext: Item on narrowest airway in child.
nursingPriority: Cricoid ring (subglottic) — implications for uncuffed ETT.

title: Lung volumes and capacities
nursingPriority: Functional Residual Capacity = ERV + RV (air after quiet expiration).

title: Larynx anatomy
keyPoints: Cartilages: thyroid, cricoid, epiglottis (single), arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform (paired)
Vocal cords between thyroid and arytenoid
Innervation: recurrent laryngeal (all intrinsic except cricothyroid)
nursingPriority: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury — voice rest, speech therapy, scope to assess cord movement.

title: Lung epithelium lining
keyPoints: Alveoli: type I (gas exchange), type II (surfactant)

title: Respiratory center stimulants
keyPoints: Central medullary: CO2 via H+ in CSF
Hypercapnia is main drive; in COPD, hypoxia becomes drive (careful O2)
clinicalContext: COPD patient on high-flow O2 with rising CO2.
nursingPriority: Titrate O2 to SpO2 88-92% to avoid loss of hypoxic drive, ABG, consider NIV if CO2 rising with acidosis.

title: Joints — types
keyPoints: Synovial subtypes: hinge, pivot, ball-and-socket, saddle, plane, condyloid

title: Types and number of bones (206)
keyPoints: Axial 80: skull 22, hyoid 1, ossicles 6, vertebrae 26, ribs 24, sternum 1

title: Bone cells — osteocytes, osteoclasts, osteoblasts
definition: Osteoblast, osteocyte, osteoclast, osteogenic stem cell.
keyPoints: Osteocyte: mature mineralized cell in lacunae

title: Largest bone (femur)
keyPoints: Common site of fracture in elderly

title: Clotting factors
keyPoints: Vit K dependent: II, VII, IX, X + proteins C, S
nursingPriority: PT (extrinsic) — INR monitors warfarin via vit K-dependent factors.

topic: Minerals required for clotting (Ca, vit K)
title: Minerals required for clotting (Ca, vit K)
keyPoints: Vit K for gamma-carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, X
Citrate chelates Ca to prevent clotting (blood bag)

title: Normal blood parameters
clinicalContext: Item on normal Hb adult male.

title: Hemopoiesis
keyPoints: Embryo: yolk sac → liver (mid-trimester) → spleen → bone marrow (by birth)
Adult: axial skeleton (vertebrae, pelvis, sternum, ribs, proximal femur)

title: Heart sounds S1-S4
keyPoints: S1: mitral + tricuspid closure (lub) — start of systole
S2: aortic + pulmonary closure (dub) — end of systole
S3: early diastolic gallop (volume overload, normal in young)
S4: late diastolic (stiff ventricle, never normal)
nursingPriority: AV valve closure at start of systole.

title: Cardiac output (CO = HR x SV)
keyPoints: Affected by preload, afterload, contractility, HR

title: Blood pressure regulation
keyPoints: Long: RAAS, ADH, ANP, sympathetic tone, kidney Na/water handling
nursingPriority: Kidney via RAAS and pressure natriuresis.

title: SA node — pacemaker
keyPoints: Location: junction of SVC and RA

title: Oxygenated vs deoxygenated blood
keyPoints: Oxygenated: pulmonary vein → LA → LV → aorta → systemic arteries
Deoxygenated: systemic veins → RA → RV → pulmonary artery (ONLY artery with deoxy blood)

title: Arterioles vs veins — diameter, resistance
keyPoints: Veins: capacitance, hold 70% blood volume, have valves (except cranial, pulmonary)

title: Agnosia
definition: Failure to recognize despite intact senses.
clinicalContext: Stroke patient cannot recognize familiar faces.
nursingPriority: Prosopagnosia — inferior temporal/occipital lesion; OT for compensatory strategies, family education.

title: Ear — anatomy
keyPoints: Middle: ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) + Eustachian tube

title: Anosmia
keyPoints: Causes: viral URI, COVID, head trauma (ethmoid fracture), Parkinson, Alzheimer early sign
clinicalContext: Patient with COVID presenting with loss of smell.
nursingPriority: Expected post-viral — usually recovers; educate; olfactory training may help.

title: Auditory pathway
keyPoints: Cochlea → CN VIII → cochlear nuclei → superior olivary complex → lateral lemniscus → inferior colliculus → medial geniculate body (thalamus) → primary auditory cortex (temporal)

title: Glomerular filtration rate (GFR)
nursingPriority: CKD stage 4 — nephrology referral, avoid nephrotoxins, dose-adjust drugs, prepare for RRT.

title: Renal tubular absorption
keyPoints: PCT: 65% Na, H2O, all glucose, amino acids, HCO3
Loop of Henle descending: water; ascending: Na/K/2Cl
clinicalContext: Item on thiazide site of action.

title: Carpal tunnel syndrome
keyPoints: Symptoms: paresthesia lateral 3.5 fingers, thenar atrophy (late), worse at night
Treatment: splint, NSAIDs, steroid injection, decompression surgery
clinicalContext: Middle-aged typist with nocturnal hand numbness.
nursingPriority: Wrist splint night-time, ergonomic modification, NSAIDs, steroid injection if refractory, EMG, surgery.

title: Foot drop
keyPoints: Common peroneal nerve (L4-S1) most common — at fibular head (crossing legs, prolonged squat)
clinicalContext: Patient with foot drop after prolonged squatting.
nursingPriority: Peroneal nerve palsy — AFO brace, avoid pressure at fibular head, PT, usually recovers.

title: Winging of scapula
keyPoints: Prominent vertebral border on arm push
Causes: radical mastectomy, blunt trauma, idiopathic
clinicalContext: Post-mastectomy with scapular prominence when pushing wall.
nursingPriority: Long thoracic nerve injury — physical therapy to strengthen remaining muscles, usually recovers.
